test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How many languages are enlisted in the eighth schedule of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The eighth schedule,** according to** Articles 344(1) and 351 of the Indian Constitution**, recognises the following **22 languages**.
 
• The official languages of India are listed in the Eighth Schedule to the Indian Constitution.
 
• Despite the fact that there are hundreds of languages spoken throughout the country, the eighth schedule recognises only** 22** as official languages.
 
• While **14** of these languages were initially included in the constitution, the remaining languages were added through subsequent changes.
 
• The Indian government is now required to take steps to help these languages evolve so that "they increase fast in richness and become effective ways of transmitting modern knowledge." 
 
• **Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri **are among the 22 languages listed in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.
 
• The Indian Constitution is divided into 12 schedules. The constitution originally included only eight schedules.
 
• **The ninth, tenth, eleventh, and twelfth schedules **were later introduced by the 1st, 52nd, 73rd, and 74th Constitutional Amendments Acts, respectively.
